prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (ideological framing removed)

- Families and education:
  - Tax changes: increase Children’s Tax Credit for under-5s; introduce a transferable Married Couple’s Allowance where there is a child under 11 or a qualifying carer; pay Working Families Tax Credit to the caring parent; remove tax on Widowed Parent benefits; create Family Scholarships for parents returning to work.
  - Schools: grant full autonomy (“Free Schools”) to heads and governors; ease exclusions and create off-site Progress Centres; direct more funding to schools by cutting bureaucracy; allow good schools to expand and new schools to be set up by parent, faith, charitable and company sponsors; give parents power to trigger Ofsted inspections and management change.
  - Students and universities: raise loan repayment threshold to £20,000; no top-up fees; create university endowments.

- Policing and justice:
  - Increase police numbers; cut bureaucracy; visible policing (“cops in shops”); create parish constables; target antisocial behaviour.
  - Expand Secure Training Centre places; link release of young offenders to qualifications/behaviour.
  - Tougher action on drug dealing to under-16s and near schools.
  - “Honesty in sentencing,” end automatic early release; require prisoners to work and contribute to victim reparation.
  - Lifetime supervision available for sex offenders; protect children online.
  - Strengthen victims’ rights; review self-defence and double jeopardy rules.

- Economy, tax and regulation:
  - £8bn in targeted tax cuts funded by savings outside schools/NHS/police/defence: abolish most taxes on savings/dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000; cut fuel duty by at least 6p/litre; introduce new married allowance; reduce business taxes; abolish IR35; simplify Capital Gains Tax.
  - Transparency: annual taxpayer statements; National Accounts Commission.
  - Regulation: Deregulation Commission with departmental regulatory budgets; exemptions for small firms; abolish Climate Change Levy; review nuclear.
  - Macroeconomy: keep the pound; bolster monetary policy institutions; keep spending growth within trend GDP.

- Health:
  - Match planned NHS funding; shift decisions to clinicians; Patient’s Guarantee of maximum waits by clinical need with choice of provider (including independent sector).
  - Restore authority to ward sisters/matrons; GP and patient choice of hospital; expand practice nurses; specialist surgical units; Exceptional Medicines Fund; raise state funding of hospices to 40%; remove tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable.

- Older people:
  - Abolish most taxes on savings; raise age-related allowance by £2,000 (about 1m removed from income tax); raise basic pension with higher uprating for over-75s; option to consolidate ancillary payments into a higher tax-free pension.
  - Explore optional funded alternative for younger workers; abolish compulsory annuitisation at 75; free nursing care; protect assets of those who pre-fund long-term care.

- Europe, defence and foreign policy:
  - Keep vetoes and the pound; seek flexible EU with reserved powers; complete single market; strengthen competition and tackle fraud.
  - Defence: meet full manning; reduce overstretch; reform reserves; cooperate on European defence only within NATO; support ballistic missile defence; maintain independent deterrent.
  - Development/trade: work towards 0.7% aid; channel more via charities (Aid Direct); push a transatlantic free trade area toward global free trade by 2020; appoint an Envoy for Religious Freedom.

- Asylum:
  - House all new applicants in secure reception centres until decisions; fast-track safe-country claims; create a Removals Agency to deport rejected cases.

- Welfare and civil society:
  - Create an Office of Civil Society; abolish irrecoverable VAT for charities (using euro-preparation funds).
  - Replace current job programmes with outcome-based “Britain Works”; “Can Work, Must Work”; expect lone parents with children over 11 to seek suitable work.
  - Improve savings rules for disabled people; new agency to pair Incapacity Benefit with rehabilitation; national anti-fraud squad; clean up National Insurance records.

- Town, country, transport, environment, culture, democracy:
  - Foot and Mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP; clear origin/method food labelling; improve animal welfare.
  - Support rural services (rate cuts, benefit card for post offices); abolish central housebuilding targets; protect waterways (“Blue Belts”).
  - Urban Regeneration Companies; support coastal towns; tackle nuisance tenants; expand homeownership (right-to-buy discounts, rent-to-mortgage, homesteading).
  - Transport: invest in roads/rail; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe; charge foreign lorries; cut fuel duty; promote cleaner vehicles.
  - Environment: meet climate goals via trading, conservation, incentives and renewables.
  - Culture/media: create cultural endowments funded by Channel 4 privatisation and lottery surplus; single communications regulator; support tourism and sport.
  - Governance: devolve powers to high-performing councils; local referendums for large council tax rises; abolish regional bodies; English votes for English laws; strengthen Lords/Commons scrutiny; reduce numbers of ministers, MPs (post-reform), and political advisers.
